subject: Subprocessor notice: SmallOps onboarding + data locality clarification
messages:
From: CloudFleet Security <security@cloudfleet.io>

Cc: SmallOps Procurement <vendor-admin@smallops.io>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor notice: SmallOps onboarding + data locality clarification

Hi Irene,

Heads up: CloudFleet is onboarding a new logging/storage vendor, SmallOps, to handle short-term log retention and indexing for our Fleet product. SmallOps will process raw logs for a subset of accounts (pilot customers) and will operate data centers in both the EU (Frankfurt) and US (Ashburn).

We understand Redwood requires notification for any subprocessor additions and flow-down of the DPA/MSA terms. Two quick asks from our side:
- Please confirm whether the existing Order Form (CF-2026-498) requires an MSA/Order Form amendment for this subprocessor addition, or if a DPA annex is sufficient.
- We need a short list of evidence items Redwood requires (SOC2 type II, encryption-at-rest details, data locality guarantee, access controls). We can provide a SOC2 snapshot and an encrypted evidence bundle.

Attached: vendor_matrix.xlsx (vendor summary), subproc_sow.pdf (scope of work).

Proposed timeline: pilot starts 2026-08-01; we need flow-down confirmation and any redline within two weeks to keep the onboarding window.

Thanks —
Ariela Gomez
CloudFleet Security
security@cloudfleet.io

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor notice: SmallOps onboarding + data locality clarification

Thanks Ariela — appreciate the heads-up. Looping in Legal (Kimberly) and Procurement (Priyom) and Contracts (Laura) to confirm the path.

High-level next steps from Redwood:
1) Legal needs to review the proposed scope and confirm whether this is a DPA-only flow-down or requires an MSA/Order Form amendment.
2) Procurement will run SmallOps through our standard supplier questionnaire and evidence capture (SOC/controls).
3) If data residency guarantees are material to the account, we'll require a rider in the DPA or a narrow Order Form clause.

Can you push the SOC2 report and any encryption/KMS architecture notes to the Drive link you provided, or attach here? Also please confirm whether SmallOps will have access to plaintext logs or only hashed/indexed tokens — that changes our required access controls.

Tentative timeline: we will triage legal redlines by 2026-07-20 if we have evidence by end of day 2026-07-15. If we need an Order Form amendment, procurement will queue DocuSign routing and notify you of impacts to the pilot start date.

If it's helpful, Kimberly, could you propose starter language for a data-locality rider we can offer to CloudFleet?

Best,
Irene Choi
Vendor Risk / Ops
Redwood Inference

On Mon, Jul 13, 2026 at 11:02 AM Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Ariela — appreciate the heads-up. Looping in Legal (Kimberly) and Procurement (Priyom) and Contracts (Laura) to confirm the path.
>
> High-level next steps from Redwood:
> 1) Legal needs to review the proposed scope and confirm whether this is a DPA-only flow-down or requires an MSA/Order Form amendment.

Thanks Irene — quick read below and a suggested starter approach.

Summary assessment:
- SmallOps appears to be a downstream processor for log ingestion/indexing only. If they will not have access to user PII or plaintext customer data beyond logs necessary for indexing, we can often proceed via a DPA amendment that explicitly references SmallOps as an authorized subprocessor and contains the required flow-down clauses (security controls, subcontractor flowdown, deletion/return obligations).
- If SmallOps will host or persist logs in the EU for EU customers and in the US for US customers, we will need an explicit data locality clause ensuring customers' EU data remain in EU infrastructure where required. That can be a DPA annex or an Order Form rider tied to specific accounts.

Required evidence (what I need to sign off):
- SOC2 Type II report (most recent 12 months).
- Encryption-at-rest details and KMS/HSM design (attestation of key separation and who has access).
- Confirmation of logging data access model (are logs stored encrypted; who can decrypt).
- Signed subprocessor clause with SmallOps agreeing to equivalent obligations and onward flow-down.

Attached: redline_subproc_clause.docx — draft language I propose to include in a DPA annex (high level):
- Data locality: "For EU customers, Logs processed by SmallOps will be stored and processed on infrastructure physically located within the European Union unless otherwise authorized in writing by Customer."
- Access controls: "SmallOps shall restrict access to Logs to personnel required to perform the Services, use KMS-backed encryption, and maintain an auditable access log retained for at least 12 months."
- Right to audit & termination: standard audit rights and right to suspend the subprocessor pending remediation.

If CloudFleet wants to accept the DPA annex, Procurement can coordinate DocuSign for Redwood + SmallOps + CloudFleet. If CloudFleet insists on an Order Form amendment, please flag the affected account(s) and we will model the rider.

Irene/Priyom — happy to triage redline language in a 20-minute sync if helpful.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: SmallOps Procurement <vendor-admin@smallops.io>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com, security@cloudfleet.io
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor notice: SmallOps onboarding + data locality clarification

Thanks Kimberly/Irene — appreciate the clear checklist and the draft language.

We can accept the DPA annex approach in principle. Responses below:
- SOC2: attached SOC2_report.pdf (snapshot) and an encrypted evidence bundle evidence_bundle.enc (password shared over separate channel).
- Data access: SmallOps will process raw logs but will not persist customer PII beyond transient processing for indexing; logs at rest are encrypted using AES-256 with keys managed in our HSM and separation-of-duties enforced.
- Data locality: SmallOps confirms we can partition EU customers to EU-only processing/storage; we will include a contractual commitment in the annex.

Next steps proposed:
1) Redwood to send the DPA annex (with Kimberly's redline) to us for counter-signature.
2) CloudFleet and SmallOps will route DocuSign (CF-2026-498) once Redwood signs — please provide the DocuSign routing order you prefer.
3) We'll complete the supplier questionnaire and accept a short audit window if required.

Attachments: SOC2_report.pdf, evidence_bundle.enc

Thanks —
Marcus Li
Head of Procurement, SmallOps
